arguments.title: Handler Security Audit with a Severity Rubric
arguments.spec:
# Handler Security Audit (analysis, not a build job)

`input/` holds four handler modules (admin-routes.mjs, search-api.mjs, session-store.mjs, webhook.mjs) plus
`input/routes.mjs`, the gateway's route table -- all READ-ONLY evidence. Do not edit anything under `input/`.
`routes.mjs` states, per handler, what a caller must already hold: `"public"`, `"session"`, or `"admin"`.
Reachability is half of every severity in this audit -- read routes.mjs and build the handler-to-auth map before
rating anything.

Deliverable `analysis/security.json` (starts `{"schemaVersion":1,"complete":false,"findings":[]}`): `findings`
holds one entry per DEFECT OCCURRENCE (not one per class -- a class with two occurrences needs two entries), each
`{file, line, kind, severity, why}`. `line` is the 1-based line that exhibits the defect. `why` explains what an
attacker gets, at least twelve characters, not a restatement of the class name.

Four classes only -- a real problem outside them is out of scope and must not be reported, because an unrecognised
kind fails the check:
- `sql_injection`: a query built by interpolating a value into a template literal handed to `db.query(...)`
  instead of passing it as a parameter. Defect line = the query line.
- `missing_authorization`: a handler routes.mjs registers with `"auth": "admin"` whose body never calls
  `requireAdmin(...)`. Defect line = the handler's declaration line. A `public` route is public by design -- not
  proving identity there is not this defect.
- `unsafe_deserialization`: caller-supplied bytes turned back into live objects via `eval`, `new Function`, or
  `vm.runInNewContext`. Defect line = the evaluating line.
- `hardcoded_secret`: a `const` whose name contains SECRET, KEY, TOKEN or PASSWORD, assigned a string literal of
  eight characters or more. A value read from the environment is not this defect.

Severity rubric: start from the class's base (`sql_injection`/`missing_authorization`/`unsafe_deserialization` =
high; `hardcoded_secret` = medium), then apply at most one modifier, first match wins: (1) the defect's ENCLOSING
function -- the nearest function declaration the defect line sits inside; a defect at module scope has none, and
a helper that a public route happens to call is not itself a public route -- is itself registered in routes.mjs
with `"auth":"public"` -> raise one step; (2) the defect is `hardcoded_secret` and its literal begins with
`sk_live_` -> raise one step; otherwise unchanged. Ladder: low -> medium -> high -> critical, capped at critical.

Frozen: `input/`, everything under `test/`, and `scripts/run-tests.mjs` are evidence, not workspace -- `npm test`
recomputes their content digests each run and fails if any moved. `test/security.test.js` DERIVES both the defect
set and its correct severity from the evidence each run (it names no file, no line, no severity), so re-deriving
them yourself IS the work; a genuine finding with an inflated or deflated rating fails exactly like an invented
one.

Set `complete` true only once every defect of these four classes is already recorded and correctly rated --
coverage is checked only at that point, and the failure message names what is still missing.

Toolchain: the sandbox is OFFLINE. Never add a dependency or test framework; `npm test` must pass exactly as-is
with the fixture's own toolchain.
arguments.plan:
Five sequential cards, one shared deliverable file (`analysis/security.json`) -- ordered so each card
starts from the previous card's committed result instead of racing it as a parallel sibling:

1. record-sql-injection -- find every db.query template-literal interpolation, rate and record each.
2. record-missing-authorization (after 1) -- find every admin-registered handler missing requireAdmin(...).
3. record-unsafe-deserialization (after 2) -- find every eval/new Function/vm.runInNewContext call site.
4. record-hardcoded-secret (after 3) -- find every SECRET/KEY/TOKEN/PASSWORD literal >=8 chars.
5. finalize-completeness (after 4) -- independently re-derive all four classes from the evidence, confirm every
   occurrence already has a correctly-rated entry, then set `complete: true`, verified by two real `npm test` runs.

Each class card: read input/routes.mjs first and build the handler-to-auth map (needed for the modifier), read the
four handler files, find every occurrence of that card's class (there may be zero, one, or more than one --
record one finding per occurrence, not one summary entry per class), compute severity via the rubric (base, then
at most one modifier), append the resulting entries, then run `npm test` before and after to confirm still green.
No card touches another class's entries or the frozen evidence paths.
arguments.summary: Splits the handler security audit into one card per defect class (SQL injection, missing admin checks, unsafe eval-based deserialization, hardcoded secrets) plus a final completeness pass, run in sequence so they safely append to the one shared JSON report instead of racing each other. 5 cards total. Each class card independently reads routes.mjs and the four handler files and computes severity via the rubric -- it does not trust any other card's ratings.
